question: Electricity thefts totalling EUR 450 million per year and progress of smart meter roll-out in Greece

The EU’s 2026 country report for Greece states that the non-technical losses in the electricity grid – which are partly to do with electricity theft, metering errors and non-payment – remain well above the EU average.

The report says that according to the Hellenic Electricity Distribution Network Operator (DEDDIE), electricity theft alone is estimated at EUR 450 million per year and increases the average households’ annual electricity bill by around EUR 60. Meanwhile, the Commission stresses that a faster roll-out of smart meters can help reduce losses. In light of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

What progress has been made with smart meter installation projects in Greece, which are supported with EU funding, and how many meters have been installed in relation to the agreed targets and timelines?
Has it noticed any delays or detected a risk of certain milestones and targets of EUfunded programmes not being achieved?
What specific measures is it asking the Greek authorities to take to rapidly reduce nontechnical losses and the financial burden passed on to diligent consumers?
